findings.title: Late bind/skip replies can repopulate the previous owner or selected queue
trigger: Owner A selects a queue and starts bindCurrent or skip.
Native completes its owner-scoped mutation and the Future response has not yet resumed Dart.
Account changes to B, so accountChanged clears current/queues/issues and increments generation.

The old Future then resumes and, before this repair, unconditionally assigns the A snapshot to current and notifies. Selecting another queue during the await causes the equivalent stale selection overwrite.
findings.evidence: Both old methods directly assigned await state.core.call(...) to current with no post-await owner/generation/alive/selected-id checks. This is an asynchronous state-write defect; no assumption of failed Native ownership validation is required.
findings.impact: Old queue names/items can reappear in the new owner controller, or replace the selected queue. No incorrect Native owner mutation or original deletion is claimed.
findings.authorization: Parent explicitly authorized only camera_downloads.dart bindCurrent/skip and corresponding controller regressions after the finding was reported.

bindCurrent.behavior: Capture owner/generation/selected-id; validate alive, not busy, same owner/generation/id and no logoutPending after status and bind reply; send captured owner/id.

skip.behavior: Require selected id at admission, capture owner/generation, and discard stale results using the same ownership/lifecycle/selection checks before current/restore.

coverage: For bind and skip: hold an already-created mutation response, change owner, release and verify no old current/queues/issues reappear, no cancel, original bytes unchanged.
For bind and skip: change selected queue while reply is held; stale response must not replace current or alter its error/binding state.
For bind and skip: the unchanged current owner/selection still accepts the correct result.
Hold camera.status during binding, change owner, release; no downloads.bind may be dispatched.

reviewedInvariants.conclusion: Connection sheet admission uses childOpen navigation lease and is no longer silently blocked by Live/Downloads exclusive state.

Explicit reconnect captures an old camera-only job before local retirement, cancels that exact id with a bounded wait, stops the global manual transfer lease, then runs a new epoch-scoped camera.connect. Mounted/epoch checks guard result/finally.
Pending requests expose cancel; a connected stale snapshot still has an explicit reconnect action, while running busy/USB work locks the action.
Live RPCs carry owner/generation admission and completion checks; matching-job finally cannot clear a newer request; pendingCameraJob exposes only camera operations.

Passive transport loss retires local state without Native cancel/stop/close; connectionRestored requires a verified distinct nonempty session and clears the retired state without auto-starting or attaching. Existing original/project lease boundaries remain.
Local queue retirement clears busy/job synchronously before generation-fenced old finally can be skipped, avoiding a lingering exclusive lock or new-run state clobber.
Manual receive has per-object busy admission, account/stopped checks around receive/import, and releases its global lease in finally. Reconnect respects the local publication boundary.
Global manual transfer arbitration uses a unique lease; stop waits only for that lease to be released, with bounded failure feedback rather than silently connecting over unfinished publication.
